subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Diabetes and Pubertal Disorders: DKA, Precocious and Delayed Puberty

steps.tx: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells driven by autoantibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase and islet cells causes absolute insulin deficiency. Peak incidence of **pediatric type 1 diabetes** occurs between five and seven years and during early adolescence. Children present with the classic osmotic triad of polyuria, secondary nocturnal enuresis in a previously toilet-trained child, polydipsia, and rapid weight loss despite polyphagia.
steps.say: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune beta-cell destruction leading to absolute insulin deficiency. Symptoms include polyuria, new bedwetting, polydipsia, and weight loss.

vis.alt: Pathophysiological flowchart displaying insulin deficiency, unrestrained lipolysis, ketone generation, and severe dehydration.
vis.caption: Metabolic cascades of absolute insulin deficiency leading to ketoacidosis and osmotic dehydration in pediatric diabetes. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Unrestrained lipolysis and free fatty acid oxidation in the setting of severe insulin deficiency generate toxic beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate. Up to forty percent of children present initially with **pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis** (DKA), defined by hyperglycemia exceeding two hundred milligrams per decilitre, venous pH below 7.30 or bicarbonate below fifteen milliequivalents per litre, and marked ketonaemia or ketonuria. Children exhibit deep sighing Kussmaul respiration.
steps.say: Diabetic ketoacidosis features hyperglycemia over two hundred, venous pH below 7.30, and serum bicarbonate below fifteen. Kussmaul breathing excretes carbon dioxide.

steps.tx: The most catastrophic neurological complication of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis carries significant mortality and long-term morbidity. Typically emerging four to twelve hours into rehydration, **cerebral oedema in DKA** presents with sudden headache, lethargy, declining Glasgow Coma Scale, bradycardia, hypertension, and pupil asymmetry. Immediate therapy mandates intravenous 3% hypertonic saline (five millilitres per kilogram over ten minutes) or intravenous mannitol (0.5 to 1.0 grams per kilogram).
steps.say: Cerebral edema during DKA therapy presents with headache, slowing heart rate, and declining consciousness. Administer three percent hypertonic saline or mannitol immediately.

left.title: Cerebral Oedema Warning Signs
points: Sudden severe headache or recurrent vomiting
Lethargy, confusion, or falling GCS score
Cushing triad: bradycardia, hypertension, apnea
Unequal or sluggishly reactive pupils; papilledema

right.title: Emergency Medical Management
points: Reduce intravenous fluid infusion rate by 50%
Administer 3% hypertonic saline (5 mL/kg over 10 min)
Or IV 20% mannitol (0.5 to 1.0 g/kg over 20 min)
Elevate head of bed to 30 degrees; intubate if comatose

steps.tx: Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis produces pubertal development before eight years in girls or nine years in boys. In **central precocious puberty**, premature pulsatile secretion of GnRH stimulates LH and FSH secretion, driving gonadal steroidogenesis and secondary sexual maturation. Idiopathic in ninety percent of girls, it is frequently secondary to hypothalamic hamartomas in boys, responding dramatically to continuous long-acting GnRH agonists like leuprolide.
steps.say: Central precocious puberty involves premature GnRH release before eight years in girls and nine in boys. Long-acting GnRH agonists halt progression and preserve final adult height.

rows: Idiopathic in girls (90%); hamartoma in boys (50%)
Normal prepubertal hormones; bone age normal

steps.tx: A unique triad of autonomous endocrine hyperfunction, distinctive cutaneous pigmentation, and fibrous osseous lesions arises from somatic mosaic activating mutations. Characterized by post-zygotic GNAS gene mutations, **McCune-Albright syndrome** features peripheral GnRH-independent precocious puberty with recurrent follicular ovarian cysts, large unilateral jagged-border cafe-au-lait skin macules (coast of Maine appearance), and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia with recurrent pathological bone fractures.
steps.say: McCune-Albright syndrome features peripheral precocious puberty, jagged coast of Maine cafe-au-lait macules, and fibrous bone dysplasia. It is caused by GNAS mosaic mutations.

left.title: Classic Diagnostic Triad
points: Autonomous peripheral precocious puberty
Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia of skeleton
Large, unilateral jagged café-au-lait pigmentation
Autonomous hyperthyroidism, Cushing, or acromegaly

right.title: Distinctive Pigmentary Morphology
points: Coast of Maine: irregular, jagged, ragged margins
Frequently respects the anatomical midline strictly
Contrast with NF-1 coast of California (smooth margins)
Overlying areas of fibrous skeletal dysplasia

steps.tx: Skin geography separates two syndromes that share a pigment name. The **coast of Maine** patch in McCune Albright syndrome has jagged, irregular edges that stop at the midline, unlike the smooth coast of California patches of neurofibromatosis. That one large unilateral patch travels with fibrous dysplasia and hormone glands that switch themselves on. Recognising the border pattern at the bedside points the whole endocrine workup in the right direction.
steps.say: A jagged coast of Maine patch stopping at the midline marks McCune Albright syndrome. Its border separates it from neurofibromatosis patches.

vis.alt: Clinical view of a large jagged edged cafe au lait patch on one side of the trunk.
vis.caption: A large unilateral patch with irregular jagged borders covers one side of the back. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Absence of secondary sexual maturation by fourteen years in boys or thirteen years in girls warrants clinical investigation. The commonest cause of delayed adolescence is **constitutional delay of growth and puberty** (CDGP), representing a benign physiological variant where family history documents late blooming in parents. Children demonstrate delayed bone age matching height age rather than chronological age, ultimately achieving normal adult height and sexual maturity.
steps.say: Constitutional delay of puberty represents late blooming with delayed bone age matching height age. A short course of low-dose testosterone or estrogen jump-starts puberty.

rows: Delayed bone age matches height age
Normal adult height matching target mid-parental

steps.tx: Benign proliferation of male glandular breast tissue occurs transiently in up to sixty percent of adolescent boys during puberty. Reversible physiological **pubertal gynaecomastia in boys** arises from a temporary imbalance between circulating estrogens and androgens during Tanner stages two and three, presenting as a tender, discrete, firm subareolar disc of glandular tissue beneath the nipple-areolar complex, resolving spontaneously within one to two years without pharmacological intervention.
steps.say: Pubertal gynecomastia affects sixty percent of adolescent boys due to temporary estrogen-androgen imbalance. A tender subareolar disc resolves spontaneously within two years.

left.title: Physiological Pubertal Gynaecomastia
points: Occurs in Tanner stages II to III (12 to 14 years)
Discrete, tender, firm subareolar glandular disc
Diameter usually measures 1 to 4 centimetres
Reassurance essential; 90% resolves within 2 years

right.title: Pathological Causes to Exclude
points: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY with small firm testes)
Adrenal or testicular estrogen-secreting tumors
Exogenous drug exposure (anabolic steroids, marijuana)
Pseudogynaecomastia: diffuse fatty tissue in obesity

steps.tx: Excessive childhood adiposity accelerates metabolic complications including insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and systemic hypertension. Driven by sedentary lifestyles and calorie-dense diets, **childhood metabolic syndrome** is defined by central abdominal obesity (waist circumference >=90th percentile) accompanied by two or more criteria: fasting triglycerides >=110 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol <=40 mg/dL, systolic/diastolic blood pressure >=90th percentile, and impaired fasting glucose.
steps.say: Childhood metabolic syndrome combines abdominal obesity with dyslipidemia, hypertension, and insulin resistance. Acanthosis nigricans provides a visible cutaneous clue.

rows: Visceral fat drives free fatty acid flux
Measure waist circumference at iliac crest
Accelerated HDL clearance in insulin resistance
Routine annual blood pressure percentile charting
